newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares fall 1.32 pct in correction.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares fall 1.32 pct in correction.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted losses in selling on Monday as the index's 1,650 support was broken in a technical correction of the recent sharp gains, brokers said.
Worries of early elections planned by end-1997 by the Islamist-led government also began to undermine sentiment again, they added.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,647, down 22 points, or 1.32 percent from Friday. It had leapt 4.6 percent last week, testing major resistance at 1,700 on Friday.
Volume shrank to 18.48 trillion lira ($129 million) from Friday's 27.31 trillion ($191 million).
"It was normal for volume to fall sharply and the index to move in a tight range today after weekend news about early elections," said Tuncay Kuzu from Sahin securities.
The troubled Islamist-conservative coalition government has begun to move towards early elections to be held by end-1997. Under Turkish law, parliament must set the polling date with a majority vote.

The ruling coalition has 274 seats in the 550-member parliament, with two seats vacant. It relies on support from a minor far right party, but analysts say even some conservative government MPs may vote against snap polls on fears they may not be reelected.

"Today's profit-taking was awaited after the recent sharp gains. The index may be squeezed in tight ranges amid weak turnover until mid-week, but I expect the market to test 1,700 level in the second half," said Serdar Karatepe from Polen securities.
The 1,700 mark is the index's all-time high close set on January 27. The 1997 intra-day high was 1,751 in January.
